note: The development engine's rules and weights (doc 24, The development engine; src/audio/music/develop/), tuned by ear in the music lab's Engine tab. candidates: how many pieces are grown per seed; keepBest: how many of the best the seed chooses among. harmony: tensionFollow, how strongly the walk prefers chords whose tension is near the phrase's target (0 ignores it); colorAmount, scales every chord's color chances (0 plain triads and sevenths only, 1 as written in the material); borrowedAmount, scales the borrowed chords and colors (the flat six, the minor iv; 0 none, 1 as written); pairPull, how strongly a color leans to its partner in material colorPairs (1 no lean); rockChance, the chance a phrase that reaches home rocks between D2 and G2 (material figures.rock); hold, scales the chance a chord lasts another bar; splitLast, the chance a phrase's last-but-one bar holds two chords (the cadence's approach arrives on the bar's later beat); returnSameCadence, multiplies the chance a returning phrase ends on the same cadence as the phrase it brings back (low, so a return changes its ending); lineChance, the chance a phrase that reaches home plays one of the material's written lines (figures.lines, such as summer's bass walk F/Eb to F/D, or Fsus4 to Fsus2 to F; spring has none), once a phrase; lineWeights multiplies each line's weight (1 keeps the material's; 0 removes it); cadenceWeights, multiplies each cadence type wherever a template offers it (1 keeps the material's weights; 0 removes it). endings: weights multiplies each ending's weight (1 keeps the material's; 0 removes it); sameAsCadence multiplies an ending whose type matches the last phrase's cadence. score: how the candidates are judged. variety rewards using many different chords; tensionFit punishes distance from the template's curve; repeatWindow punishes a run of four chords that comes back (a loop); stuck punishes the same chord three bars running; colorCrowd punishes more than colorCrowdShare of bars on color chords; roughReturn punishes a return that starts on a chord the grammar cannot reach from the one before it (a phrase may always start again at home, on I); bars a return keeps on purpose are not counted as loops; bannedLoops are sequences (by place) never allowed, such as I V vi IV.

melody.note: Phase 4b, the melody (src/audio/music/develop/song.js, melody.js, fit.js, critic.js, counter.js). chance: how often a grown piece sings, by weather or slot (default for the rest); the others stay chords and bed. candidates: melodies grown per piece; keepBest: how many of the best the seed chooses among. techniques: how often each development technique follows a phrase's motif (doc 24); lean multiplies them by slot or weather (evenings and mist slower, diminution mornings only). pools: which motif roles each kind of phrase opens with, best first (a phrase's kind comes from its role: statement and call open, answer answers, climb, peak, development and turn climb, cadence closes). headDevelop: the chance a climbing phrase develops the piece's first motif rather than taking a new one. overChance: the chance a motif written over a chord line (summer's sus turn over Fsus4, Fsus2, F) is sung where that line plays. register: lowest and highest MIDI note, by weather or slot (evenings stay under the frogs). breath: eighths of rest after each phrase's goal note, per meter. dynamics: the opening dynamic. counter: the counter-line under the melody in answer phrases (summer's guitar, or the vibraphone with the electric piano); chance per singing piece, register, enterLate (the chance it waits out the phrase's first bar), breath. score: the critic's weights (critic.js): leaps (a leap of a fourth or more not stepped back from), repeats (a note three times running), steps (distance of the share of steps from stepShare), rhythm (a few note lengths), range (semitones over a tenth in a phrase), highPoints (a phrase's top note struck twice), motifShare (distance of the motif's share from motifTarget), tension (phrases peak higher where the template is tenser), frogBandWeight (evening and night notes inside frogBand, MIDI), parallels (fifths or octaves with the bass at two chord changes running).
